title: R4306: Dutch diplomatic cipher, transcribed with CTTS and solved with Opus 5.5

documents.shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Stockholm, Chifferklaver låda II:133; DECODE R4306
documents.date: Undated; pencilled 1632?; references letters of 23 February and 13 March
documents.route: Unknown sender → unknown recipient; Amsterdam reported by earlier survey, unverified here

plaintext.source: No interlinear or marginal decipherment on the supplied cipher page. No historical plaintext or matched archive key used in the contributed solution.

transcription.source: George Lasry’s CTTS project; Codex merged separated digit boxes; current post-review transcription supplied with the Opus 5.5 solution.
transcription.notes: 35 CTTS rows, 463 selections; two date-numeral selections (285=23, d13=13) excluded from cipher counts. Position-label histogram matches transcription exactly. DECODE lists three record pages; only this one cipher page is submitted.

system.summary: An alphabetical numerical substitution, 30–52, with nulls and four unresolved three-digit nomenclator codes.

diacritics.note: Dots/colons separate numbers; superscript marks on date numerals do not select a cipher alphabet.

system.doubled_letters: Encoded twice; no general doubling operator established.
system.sibling_key: No archive or sibling key used. Earlier survey tested R4296 and R4310 unsuccessfully.
system.notes: 23 alphabet positions (30–52), 21 observed; 45=q and 51=x are predictions. Source header calls this 24 letters but lists only 23. Fifteen observed null classes (34 occurrences), plus unobserved null 13 in the source key. No j, v or z assignment. Date labels 285 and d13 represent literal 23 and 13; they are not nomenclator entries.

prior_solution.where: The 21 September repository survey reports failed attempts; DECODE is still Non-decrypted on 17 October 2026. No prior plaintext was located in the limited exact-phrase search; no priority claim.

conditions.human_role: George Lasry directed the work, supplied the CTTS material, and supplied the edited Dutch reading, English translation and contextual notes. He confirms: transcribed with CTTS, then solved with Opus 5.5. Codex packaged the PR and checked counts, glyphs and five mechanical lines.
tools: Codex digit-box merging and contribution checks
build.py (counts, visual key, five-line mechanical excerpt only)

solution.what: Earlier riksarkivet1628 survey reports failed numerical attacks in multiple languages and rejected keys R4296/R4310. These are prior attempts, not new runs in this contribution.
CTTS digit selections were merged into numerical units; current supplied snapshot contains 463 selections in 35 rows. Subsequent sign corrections are recorded in the preserved source-key comments.

George Lasry confirms that Opus 5.5 solved the cipher after CTTS transcription. The working-key header describes crib dragging; the result is an alphabetical number mapping with nulls. No historical plaintext or external key supplied the recovery. Exact prompts and run settings are not reconstructed.

Matched all 463 position labels to transcription counts; counted 461 cipher elements after excluding date numerals, and reapplied the current key to exactly five manuscript lines without correcting their spelling.

Checked public DECODE metadata: Riksarkivet Chifferklaver låda II:133, three record pages, broad 1600–1699 catalogue range, blank correspondents/languages and Non-decrypted status. Image manager requires login; only the supplied cipher page is independently inspected here.

validation.notes: The requested five manuscript lines contain only 62 literal letters, below the validator minimum of 80; no full mechanical decryption is included. No statistical accuracy claim is made.

outcome.method_basis: Transcribed with CTTS, then solved with Opus 5.5, as confirmed by George Lasry; no historical plaintext or external key used.
outcome.fraction_read_source: counts.json: 422 assigned letter occurrences / 427 non-null cipher occurrences. Five unresolved code occurrences; 34 nulls and two date-numeral selections excluded. Assignment coverage, not verified meaningful-reading accuracy.

credits.note: Directed the work and supplied the CTTS project, edited Dutch text, translation and context. Transcribed with CTTS, then solved with Opus 5.5.

gaps.detail: Four identities unresolved in five occurrences. Context suggests persons, powers or courts; identities are not supplied.
gekl…men, [v]ersoeck, ga[d]e, Mar[t]y and the final sentence remain editorial or uncertain; the five-line excerpt preserves literal ekll and alsodesaecken.
Pencilled 1632? is not an established document date. The older survey reports Amsterdam on another view, not verified from the contributed page.

outcome.notes: Belongs to: Riksarkivet key-box and Oxenstierna ciphers. Exactly five mechanical lines included; the full Dutch reading and translation are supplied editions. No full mechanical decryption or established year/identity claimed.
